author: reek
body: A hex digit reads by literal comparison, both cases accepted, and a character that is no hex digit answers minus one so the decoder can tell a real escape from a stray percent.

author: reek
body: The explore form carries exactly three keys: dim, repeated once per checked dimension, meas, repeated once per checked measure, and limit. Repeated dim and meas values gather in arrival order, an empty value is dropped rather than passed to the planner as a ghost name, a later limit wins over an earlier one, and every other key is ignored. The limit accepts nothing but digits: an absent, empty, or garbage limit is zero, which the planner reads as no limit.

author: reek
body: Pairs split on the first equals sign only, so a value carrying an encoded equals sign survives whole. A pair with no equals sign is a bare key with the empty value, which the field reader then ignores.
